name: Time-series forecasting and analysis

conventions.text: Draw the series themselves as data: thin line plots of the actual input (and output) curves, in small framed strips or on bare Value/Time axes, rather than an icon or a box labelled 'time series'.
Show patching on the curve itself: cut the drawn series into consecutive dotted or dashed rectangles, one per patch, and run one arrow from each window up into its token.
Mark the look-back/horizon split on the input: a vertical divider with an empty 'to predict' region, greyed-out forecast patches, or decoder cells printed with 0 for the horizon.
Give a multivariate input one strip or plot per variate (stacked strips or side-by-side plots, or a dashed box around each whole curve) so channels read as separate units before they enter the model.
Give each variate its own colour on its curve and keep that colour on its tokens downstream, so which channel a token came from is read from colour.

Draw tokens as a row of small separate equal cells, squares or bars between the curve and the model; print the token's content in it when it is discrete (integer IDs) and use ellipses for the long middle.
Show masked patches in the token row itself: a grey '[mask]' bar or an empty dashed outline in place of the patch, and draw reconstructed or predicted outputs only above those positions.
Stack patch-token models bottom-to-top: the series or input band at the base, then full-width layer bands rising above it, with the token columns running straight up through every band.
Use one colour for observed context and another for predicted values on both curves and tokens (e.g. blue context, red/pink forecast; green input series, blue output series).
Draw probabilistic outputs as distributions: filled density curves above the forecast positions, probability bars on a value axis, or a light band around the forecast curve.

Draw a decomposition forecaster as an encoder container above a decoder container with one wire dropping between them, and give the trend its own bottom lane in the decoder that accumulates each decomposition block's output through circled pluses.

In a teaser, start from one drawn series and show the new view of it on the curve itself (bars across time steps vs boxes around whole variates; period segments stacked as offset copies) before any model block.

Give the paper's key two-way distinction two saturated colours, red and blue, and repeat them on curve overlays, token outlines, labels and gradient arrows; keep the rest of the figure pastel or grey.

Label tensors with their time-series dimensions (variates × length, patch length × number of patches, L → L/2 → L/4, ℝ vs ℂ after a Fourier transform) inside or beside each block or along a margin axis.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
